stories.title: BIP-110 Bitcoin fork chain stalls at two blocks as miners boycott it
stories.summary: BIP-110, a contested Bitcoin soft-fork proposal, entered mandatory signaling this week with backing from under 3% of miners. It briefly split Bitcoin into two chains, but the branch enforcing BIP-110 mined only two blocks before an apparent miner boycott halted its progress, and the gap between it and the main chain has continued to widen.
stories.whyItMatters: A fork attempt with almost no miner support stalling out is a real-time test of how Bitcoin's decentralized governance handles unilateral protocol changes pushed without broad consensus.
whatToWatch: Whether the BIP-110 chain resumes mining or is effectively abandoned
Statements from miners, pools, or exchanges on which chain they'll support
Any warnings about replay or double-spend risk during the split
Developer commentary on BIP-110's technical fate
questions: What change did BIP-110 actually propose, and who championed it without majority miner buy-in?
Will any exchanges list or credit the minority chain?

stories.title: Bitcoin's BIP-110 fork mines two blocks, then halts
stories.summary: The controversial BIP-110 Bitcoin soft-fork attempt produced two blocks on its own chain before mining activity on that branch stopped, according to an early CoinDesk report. The halt came shortly after the fork's mandatory signaling period began with only a small sliver of miner support.
stories.whyItMatters: It's an early signal that a fork lacking broad miner backing may fail to gain traction, which matters for anyone tracking risks to Bitcoin's network stability.
whatToWatch: Whether mining on the BIP-110 branch resumes
Follow-up reporting on why the branch stopped
questions: Was the halt due to lack of miners or a technical issue?

stories.title: Wall Street has put $7B into tokenized funds — but almost none of it touches DeFi
stories.summary: Institutional investors have moved roughly $7 billion into tokenized funds, but new data cited by CryptoSlate shows less than 1% of that capital is actually being used within DeFi protocols. The finding suggests tokenization adoption on Wall Street is happening largely in isolation from the on-chain ecosystem it was expected to plug into.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a reality check on the narrative that institutional tokenization automatically fuels DeFi activity — the capital and the on-chain utility appear to be two separate stories.
whatToWatch: Whether tokenized-fund issuers build more DeFi-compatible use cases
Any regulatory clarity on using tokenized funds as on-chain collateral
questions: What's specifically blocking tokenized fund holders from deploying into DeFi?
Which funds and issuers make up the $7 billion figure?

stories.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs pull in $853M, with BlackRock's IBIT leading
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $853 million in net inflows, with BlackRock's IBIT capturing the largest share, per CoinDesk. The inflow points to renewed institutional appetite for regulated Bitcoin exposure.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows remain one of the clearest read-throughs on institutional demand for Bitcoin, and IBIT's continued dominance underscores BlackRock's outsized influence on that demand.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows continue in coming daily/weekly reports
Flow comparisons across competing spot Bitcoin ETFs
questions: Is this inflow part of a sustained streak or a one-off spike?
What drove the specific timing of this demand?

stories.title: Brazil orders crypto exchanges to delay large overseas transfers by up to 24 hours
stories.summary: Brazil's central bank has ordered crypto exchanges to hold large crypto transfers sent abroad for up to 24 hours, aiming to give authorities a window to catch fraud before funds leave the country. The rule specifically targets outbound crypto flows rather than all transactions.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete regulatory intervention in one of Latin America's biggest crypto markets and could become a template for other regulators worried about cross-border fraud and capital flight.
whatToWatch: Implementation timeline and compliance guidance for exchanges
Effect on outbound transfer volumes
Whether other central banks consider similar transfer holds
questions: What transfer size or risk criteria trigger the hold?
How will exchanges assess fraud risk within the window?

stories.title: Crypto 'audited' badges are giving investors a false sense of security, analysis warns
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate analysis argues that crypto projects' 'audited' badges often overstate the protection they offer, since audits can have narrow scope, go stale, or be commissioned and paid for by the project itself. The piece warns investors treat these badges as a blanket safety guarantee even though real risks — like admin-key exploits or uncovered logic bugs — can slip through.
stories.whyItMatters: Audit badges are a widely used trust signal in a market plagued by hacks and rug pulls, so an unreliable signal leaves investors under-protected without realizing it.
whatToWatch: Whether audit firms respond to the criticism
Any push for standardized audit scope or disclosure requirements
questions: Which specific incidents or audits prompted this analysis?
Are there concrete proposals to close the disclosure gap?

stories.title: Bitwise's Solana ETF drew $267M in inflows — then market losses wiped it out
stories.summary: Bitwise's Solana ETF pulled in roughly $267 million from investors, but a subsequent decline in Solana's price erased those gains, leaving the fund's value little changed despite the fresh capital. It's a reminder that strong inflows don't insulate a fund from the underlying asset's price moves.
stories.whyItMatters: It highlights the added volatility risk of newer altcoin ETFs and pushes back on narratives that treat inflows alone as evidence of a healthy investment.
whatToWatch: Solana's price trajectory in coming weeks
Subsequent flow data for the ETF
Performance comparisons with other altcoin ETFs
questions: What specifically drove the Solana price decline during this period?

stories.whyItMatters: As more investors lean on AI tools for portfolio guidance, an undisclosed bias toward a volatile asset like Bitcoin could influence decisions without users knowing it's there.

stories.title: Saylor says ChatGPT helped Strategy unlock $15B in Bitcoin-buying capacity

stories.whyItMatters: Strategy is one of the largest corporate Bitcoin holders, so any expansion of its buying capacity is meaningful for institutional BTC demand.

stories.title: Bitcoin treasury firm Empery sells 1,635 BTC, cutting reserves 76% in weeks
stories.summary: Empery offloaded about 1,635 BTC, shrinking its Bitcoin reserves by roughly 76% over just a few weeks — a sharp break from the 'never sell' corporate treasury philosophy popularized by firms like Strategy. The sale suggests at least some corporate Bitcoin holders are more willing to liquidate than the dominant narrative around treasury companies suggests.
stories.whyItMatters: It tests the durability of the accumulate-and-never-sell corporate Bitcoin treasury model that has underpinned a chunk of institutional BTC demand.
whatToWatch: Whether other Bitcoin treasury companies follow with sales of their own
Any stated rationale from Empery for the liquidation
Effects on valuation premiums of publicly traded treasury companies
questions: Why did Empery sell — liquidity needs, risk management, or a change in conviction?

stories.title: Hyperliquid's RWA perps boom may be eating into revenue that backs HYPE
stories.summary: Growing trading volume in real-world-asset perpetual futures on Hyperliquid is reportedly cutting into the protocol revenue that ultimately supports its HYPE token, according to CoinDesk, since RWA perps carry different fee economics than the platform's core crypto perps. The shift raises questions about how HYPE's value-accrual model holds up as the platform's business mix changes.
stories.whyItMatters: HYPE's valuation has been closely tied to Hyperliquid's revenue-sharing mechanics, so a change in revenue composition could directly affect token holders.

Whether the protocol adjusts incentives to rebalance the mix
HYPE price and valuation reaction
questions: How exactly do RWA perps' fees or revenue split differ from standard crypto perps?

stories.title: Crypto is seeing a dot-com-style shakeout, with over 100 projects folding in 2026
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports the crypto industry is going through a shakeout reminiscent of the dot-com bust, with more than 100 projects shutting down so far in 2026. The wave of failures points to a thinning-out of speculative or unsustainable ventures left over from the last market cycle.
stories.whyItMatters: A large die-off of projects can be read either as a healthy market correction clearing out weak players or as a warning sign of deeper capital and revenue problems across the sector.
whatToWatch: Whether the pace of shutdowns accelerates or slows through the rest of 2026
